title: Problem Overview
content: Erdős Problem #1088: Guaranteed Distinct Distance Subsets. Status: OPEN

title: Alldistancesdistinct
content: A set of points in ℝ^d where all pairwise distances are distinct. We represent points as functions Fin d → ℝ. ∀ p₁ p₂ q₁ q₂ : Fin d → ℝ, p₁ ∈ S → p₂ ∈ S → q₁ ∈ S → q₂ ∈ S → ({p₁, p₂} : Set (Fin d → ℝ)) ≠ {q₁, q₂} → p₁ ≠ p₂ → q₁ ≠ q₂ → Finset.sum Finset.univ (fun i => (p₁ i - p₂ i)^2) ≠ Finset.sum Fi

title: F
content: f_d(n): the minimal m such that every set of m points in ℝ^d contains an n-point subset with all pairwise distances distinct.

title: One Dim Bound
content: ∃ c₁ c₂ : ℝ, c₁ > 0 ∧ c₂ > 0 ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, n ≥ 1 → c₁ * (n : ℝ)^2 ≤ (f 1 n : ℝ) ∧ (f 1 n : ℝ) ≤ c₂ * (n : ℝ)^2

title: Erdos Straus Upper Bound
content: ∃ c : ℝ, c > 1 ∧ ∀ d : ℕ, d ≥ 1 → (f d n : ℝ) ≤ c ^ d

title: Subexponential Conjecture
content: **Erdős's Question (OPEN)**: For fixed n ≥ 3, is f_d(n) = 2^{o(d)}?  Equivalently: does log₂(f_d(n)) / d → 0 as d → ∞? The Erdős-Straus bound gives log₂(f_d(n)) ≤ C_n · d, so the question asks whether this can be improved to sublinear growth. ∀ n : ℕ, n ≥ 3 → ∀ ε : ℝ, ε > 0 → ∃ D : ℕ, ∀ d : ℕ, d ≥ D

title: Erdos 1088
content: Known: f_d(n) ≤ c_n^d (exponential upper bound). Open: Is f_d(n) = 2^{o(d)}? ∃ c : ℝ, c > 1 ∧ ∀ d : ℕ, d ≥ 1 → (f d n : ℝ) ≤ c ^ d := erdos_straus_upper_bound n hn
